title: The relative section component has geometrically irreducible fibres
statement: Let $g:P\to T$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], quasi-compact and quasi-separated morphism of schemes with a section $\sigma:T\to P$. There is an open $U\subset P$ containing the range of $\sigma$ such that $U\to T$ has geometrically irreducible fibres and contains every point in the fibre connected component through the section.

source.place: Tag 055R for openness; Tag 04KV for rational-point geometric connectedness; Tag 0EY4 for smooth slicing

proof.text: Define U to be exactly the set of points in the fibre component through the section. Its openness is lem-sbc-smooth-section-component-open. The section identity puts every section point in U by reflexive membership in its component; lift the section through the open immersion U into P.

For each t, compose the fibre inclusion of U into U with U into P. Its image is exactly the connected component of sigma(t) in the fibre over t: one inclusion follows from the defining predicate of U, and the other follows from the fibre-image criterion and membership in U. This map is an embedding. Its homeomorphism to its image identifies the fibre with the nonempty connected component, proving ConnectedSpace of that fibre.

Base change the restricted section to each residue field, using pullback.lift. Apply the already proved library theorem GeometricallyConnected.of_connectedSpace_of_section (Stacks 04KV), then the Mathlib fibre criterion to obtain geometric connectedness of U over T. After any base change to a field the source is connected, smooth and locally noetherian. Smooth.isRegularLocalRing_stalk makes each stalk regular; IsRegularLocalRing.isDomain makes it a domain. The already proved irreducibleSpace_of_isDomain_stalk gives irreducibility. This is precisely GeometricallyIrreducible. Finally the required component containment is the defining predicate of U.
